title: CI slack for the two perf budgets without one. tests/perf/budgets.test.ts holds
input: CI slack for the two perf budgets without one. tests/perf/budgets.test.ts holds a rebuild's write transaction at 2000 entries to 50 ms on one measurement, and tests/perf/semantic.test.ts holds the median of a global search by meaning over 65000 memories to 40 ms, with no slack on CI, while the hook budgets in the same file hold the median with a 2.5 slack on a CI runner (CI=1). On GitHub's macos-latest runner the rebuild took 70, 59 and 64 ms and the search 47 ms in three runs of PR 35 and in the push run of #34, so check (macos-latest) fails and the ruleset blocks the merge. The fix: the rebuild is measured five times and its median held, and both budgets carry the file's SLACK (2.5 on CI, 1 on a developer's machine), so the budgets on a developer's machine stay 50 ms and 40 ms.
routeReasons: chore in one spot, clear request, no risk area

criteria.text: With CI=1 the two tests announce and hold the budgets with the slack (the rebuild median of five measurements under 125 ms, the semantic median under 100 ms); without CI they announce 50 ms and 40 ms: checked by running both tests with and without CI=1 and reading the names and the measured lines
The two perf tests keep passing on this machine with the budgets unchanged at 50 ms (the rebuild) and 40 ms (the semantic median) when CI is unset
